Writeups / Reverse engineering

Reverse engineering

Processor Architectures and Binary Analysis

Planned studies of IoT processor architectures, memory layout, and calling conventions, connecting C/C++ programs with their compiled machine code.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned work covers ARM, MIPS, RISC-V, and Xtensa, including Xtensa-based ESP32 devices. Analysis will connect memory layout and calling conventions to C/C++ code, using Ghidra, IDA Pro or Binary Ninja, and radare2/rizin.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Architecture survey

  • Compare ARM, MIPS, RISC-V, and Xtensa conventions relevant to IoT firmware.
  • Record endianness, register width, and memory layout per target.
  • Select one architecture for a worked example.

Toolchain and loader

  • Identify the image format and load address.
  • Set up the disassembler or decompiler with the correct processor profile.
  • Verify function boundaries against known entry points.

Memory layout and calling conventions

  • Map code, data, stack, and heap regions.
  • Document argument passing, return values, and stack frames.
  • Connect C/C++ constructs to the generated instructions.

Static analysis workflow

  • Annotate imported functions and library code.
  • Rename structures and variables as understanding improves.
  • Cross-reference strings, constants, and peripheral addresses.

Worked example and references

  • Document one function from source-level intent to machine code.
  • Record tools, versions, and unresolved questions.
  • Link the relevant architecture manuals and ABI documents.

Topics to cover

  • ARM, MIPS and RISC-V
  • Xtensa and ESP32
  • Memory layout and calling conventions
  • Ghidra and IDA Pro / Binary Ninja
  • radare2/rizin
